thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: URGENT: High GPU driver resets (Xid) detected on prod-inference-3. Severity: P1. 30% of GPU nodes reporting driver reset in last 5m. Pager -> marie, ajay. Logs attached to incident ticket: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2027

marie: I’m on it. starting triage — which pool is flapping?

ajay: prod-inference-3 (us-west-2a) - affected nodes: gnode-7, gnode-9, gnode-12. Xid counts: gnode-7: 46, gnode-9: 22, gnode-12: 57 in last 10m. seeing driver reset + container restarts. latency spikes on /v1/generate :

ajay: dmesg snippet:
```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, PID: 10234, GPU:0
[ 12345.679012] NVRM: GPU at 0x0000:65:00: driver reset
[ 12345.689000] kernel: GPU ECC error detected on GPU0
```

marie: thanks. are affected pods being rescheduled or OOMing?

ajay: mix — some pods crash on driver reset (OOM not primary), others hit CUDA errors in runtime: `CUBLAS_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR`. Containers rapidly restart; requests 5xx -> spike in errors to customers hitting medium-size models.

tess: tagging eng-runtime (@josh) and infra (@infra-bot) — please join.

josh: on it. first ask: any kernel/driver change recently?

ajay: We rolled driver 525.60 -> 525.85 on 2078499000 (yesterday morning) across the cluster. Rollout was partial to canary then global. These nodes show the newer driver.

infra-bot: Observability: GPU ECC errors correlate with nodes that have higher memory utilization + long-running KV cache hotlines. Top processes: model-server (pid 10234), cache-writer.

marie: mitigation plan: 1) take affected nodes OOS (cordon+drain) one at a time, 2) route traffic to fallback model variants (lower memory), 3) enable auto-fallback policy for 20m, 4) open hw ticket if ECC continues. Doing 1 now on gnode-12.

marie: Command I ran:
```
kubectl cordon gnode-12 && kubectl drain gnode-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

ajay: confirming drain started. Moving pods -> fallback pool. Will also bump replica count for small-model pool by +10 to absorb traffic.

cs-sam: CS note: We’ve seen ~12 customers with elevated 5xx, mostly short-lived. Notifying top 3 enterprise customers with ETA ~30m for mitigation. Posting status on portal.

marie: switched route policy to fallback for impacted routes: `route:prod-inference -> model:small` (temporary).

kevin: +1 to draining. For each node we confirm driver reset count stops after removal. If still happening on healthy nodes we need to rollback driver.

ajay: quick check on gnode-12 after cordon: driver resets stopped on node once traffic drained (few more residual resets but no new spikes). gnode-7 & gnode-9 still flapping.

josh: can you capture full kernel logs and `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,ERR` output before we reprovision? Also capture model server core dumps if any.

ajay: uploading logs to incident ticket: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2027/logs/2078502468.tar.gz

marie: short-term: continuing rolling drain for gnode-7 and gnode-9. If drain does not reduce resets we’ll pin traffic to dedicated fallback capacity and schedule a driver rollback to 525.60 for the canary subset.

infra-bot: hardware telemetry: ECC correctable counts increased 4x on gnode-12 in last 6h. Suggest hardware inspection if persistent.

marie: CS update posted, mitigation in progress. Current SLO impact: 0.8% global 5xx bump, peak 3% for affected routes.

kevin: when marie steps off shift (ETA 22:00 PST) I’ll take primary. marie — anything you want me to watch specifically?

marie: handoff checklist for kevin: 1) ensure drains complete on gnode-7/9, 2) confirm fallback routing remains enabled, 3) check infra ticket for ECC telemetry, 4) if resets persist after rollback window (30m) open ENG-RUNTIME hotfix/rollback. Link: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2027/handbook

kevin: got it. I’ll be on for the next 4h. If Xid resets continue after all nodes drained and driver rollback didn’t help, escalate to hardware vendor and open a full maintenance window.

marie: thanks everyone :thumbsup: will update incident timeline and start RCA doc.

josh: putting note: potential root causes to investigate — driver regression in 525.85 interacting with long-lived KV caches and ECC hot pages; kernel scheduling edge-case. Will reproduce on staging with enabled stress test.

cs-sam: final note for CS: customers on SRE status page updated. Will coordinate outreach after final impact numbers.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2027 status updated: Mitigation in progress, Severity P1 -> Partial mitigation. Next update in 20m or on change.
